name: Karnak Temple Complex
kingdom: New Kingdom of Egypt (The Imperial Age)
builtBy: Pharaohs Senusret I to Ramesses II
description: The largest religious sanctuary of the ancient world, featuring the colossal Great Hypostyle Hall with 134 towering sandstone columns.
history: Dedicated to the Theban triad of Amun, Mut, and Khonsu, it served as the political and religious epicenter of the Egyptian Empire.
construction: Spans over 100 hectares with sandstone blocks transported down the Nile from Gebel el-Silsila.
architecture: Features monumental pylons, towering obelisks of Hatshepsut, and the Hypostyle Hall with columns rising 21 meters high.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979; the pinnacle of Egyptian temple architecture.
currentStatus: Standing and open to the public in Luxor, Egypt.
